model: BVPS compounding x exit P/B (insurer/reinsurer holdco, dividends + terminal exit discounted at cost of equity)

inputs.fy0: Q3 2026 balance sheet (30 Sep 2026); projection years are 12-month periods ending 30 September
inputs.wacc_rationale: Not a WACC engine -- Arch is a holding company earning underwriting profit and investment income, and the flows modelled (ROE on common equity, dividends, an exit at a book multiple) are already after financing cost, so debt is NOT deducted (subtracting it from a post-financing equity flow double counts it). Leverage is no longer trivial, though: after the June 2026 $2.0bn senior note issue, senior notes are $4,286m and preferred $830m against $22,162m of common equity (debt plus preferred about 19% of total capital, up from about 13% at December 2025), while $3.4bn of stock was bought back in nine months. Discount rate is cost of equity in USD, built as ~4.3% 10yr UST + ~5.2pp equity risk premium at an insurance-underwriting beta of ~0.9-1.0: 9.0% bull / 9.5% base / 10.5% bear. UNCHANGED from the prior version; a sustained 50bp+ move in the 10-year Treasury, or a rating-agency reaction to the higher leverage, is what would move it.
inputs.lease_treatment: not applicable -- insurance holdco, no owner-FCF component build
inputs.nci_treatment: not applicable -- Arch has no material non-controlling interests; wholly owned subsidiaries
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE (unchanged from the prior version): routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md row 'Insurer, holdco, compounder-of-book' -> BVPS compounding x exit P/B, matching the Fairfax (FRFHF) precedent. An owner-FCF DCF is wrong for an insurer: operating cash flow is dominated by float movements, EBITDA is not meaningful for an underwriting business, and capital adequacy rather than net debt is the balance-sheet story. The model compounds COMMON equity at an ROE path (applied to beginning-of-year common equity), pays a ~4% common payout, spends a stated fraction of retained earnings on buybacks at a price-to-book that glides linearly from today's multiple to the scenario exit multiple, and values the share as PV(dividends) + PV(Year-5 BVPS x exit P/B) at the cost of equity. THIS UPDATE (2026-11-19) is an anchor refresh; no scenario driver path was re-judged. Anchors moved from the Q2 2026 to the Q3 2026 10-Q: book value per share 68.04 -> 67.90, common equity 22,162 (GAAP equity 22,992 less 830 of Series F and G preferred), period-end shares 326.4m. Two anchor errors in the prior version are corrected: it used 348.8m shares, which was the Q2 weighted-average diluted count rather than the 341.0m period-end count behind the disclosed BVPS, and so back-solved common equity of 23,732 and 'implied preferred' of 298 where the filing shows 23,200 and 830. Because the model works per share from disclosed BVPS, those two errors scaled out and are worth nothing in the bridge. Book value per share fell in Q3 despite an 18.1% annualized ROE because unrealized losses on the available-for-sale portfolio took $657m (about $2.00/share) through AOCI and $1,433m of buybacks at an average $96.65 (1.42x book) cost about $1.30/share of book; AOCI stands at -$1,076m, so BVPS excluding it is about $71.20. starting_pb_for_buybacks is the market price-to-book at the valuation date and moved 1.40 -> 1.60 with the share price; it is an anchor, not a judgment, and it is the larger part of the change in value because every modelled buyback now retires fewer shares. EVIDENCE WEIGHED AND DELIBERATELY NOT ACTED ON: (1) ROE paths. Nine-month 2026 annualized net ROE was 18.2% and operating ROE 15.8% (Q3: 18.1% / 16.0%), bracketing the base Year-1 16.5%. Net earned premium is down 6% year on year and reinsurance net written premium down 9% in Q3, and the mortgage combined ratio has drifted from 14.6% (FY2025) to 25.5%, all consistent with the glide to a 13% mid-cycle ROE already in the base path. A full-year operating ROE outside roughly 14-18%, or adverse casualty reserve development, would move Year 1-2. (2) Buyback fractions. Actual repurchases ran at about 110% of nine-month earnings (139% in Q3), well above the base 75%, partly funded by the June note issue; but only $725m of authorisation remained at quarter end and October repurchases slowed to $102m with the stock at a higher multiple. The path is left alone; a new multi-billion authorisation would move Year 1. In this model buybacks near the exit multiple are close to value-neutral, so the sensitivity is low. (3) Payout 4%. Arch declared no common dividend in the nine months (retained earnings show only $30m of preferred dividends); its common distributions have been occasional specials. The 4% is kept as a prior judgment standing in for those; setting it to zero changes value by cents. (4) Exit P/B 1.00 / 1.35 / 1.60. The stock now trades at the bull exit multiple; nothing in the Q3 filing bears on where the multiple settles in five years.
inputs.share_count_basis: 326.4m common shares and common share equivalents net of treasury at 30 Sep 2026 -- the denominator of Arch's own disclosed $67.90 book value per share (Q3 2026 10-Q book-value table). Excludes 8.1m stock options and 0.4m restricted/performance units; their treasury-method dilution is not modelled (unchanged simplification from the prior version, worth roughly 0.5-1% of BVPS). A further ~1.1m shares ($102m) were repurchased 1-30 Oct 2026 and are not in the anchor.
inputs.net_debt_note: net_debt is 0 by the non-FCF-model convention (equity flows discounted at cost of equity; debt is not deducted a second time), not because Arch is debt-free: senior notes were $4,286m and preferred shares $830m at 30 Sep 2026.
inputs.buyback_cash_note: Shares repurchased for treasury, nine months to 30 Sep 2026 (equity statement); $1,433m of it in Q3 at an average $96.65. $725m of authorisation remained at 30 Sep 2026.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: equity_5yr_cagr (BVPS CAGR, most conservative of the three and the anchor for an insurer valued on book-value compounding)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Revenue (18.6%/5yr) and EPS (28.4%/5yr) both run well above BVPS growth (15.1%/5yr) because FY2023-2025 was a historic hard market (record combined ratios in the low-80s%) atop a much smaller premium base after the 2022 cat-loss trough; none of the three trailing CAGRs should be extrapolated forward given the explicit 2026 softening-cycle guidance in the Analysis JSON (property-cat rate-on-line down up to 25% at June 2026 renewals). Forward ROE/BVPS growth assumptions below are set materially below all three trailing CAGRs for this reason.

base.narrative: ROE glides from 16.5% (still-firm Reinsurance/Mortgage segments, Insurance absorbing elevated cat losses) to a mid-cycle 13% by Year 5 as 2026-2027 property-cat renewals reprice down; buyback pace tapers from ~75% to 60% of retained earnings as capital competes with organic growth in casualty and MidCorp/Entertainment; exit multiple 1.35x roughly matches today's 1.40x, i.e. no re-rating assumed, only compounding.
base.starting_pb_note: Market price-to-book at the valuation date (current_price / book_value_per_share); refreshed with the price, not judged.

bull.narrative: Cat losses stay benign, casualty firming offsets property-cat softening, Mortgage segment remains a stable high-margin ballast, and disciplined cycle management (the core moat per Analysis JSON) keeps consolidated ROE in the mid-to-high teens through the horizon; sustained ROE justifies a re-rate to 1.60x book, in line with peer premium multiples (RenaissanceRe, Everest) at cycle peaks.
bull.starting_pb_note: Market price-to-book at the valuation date (current_price / book_value_per_share); refreshed with the price, not judged.

bear.narrative: Property-cat softening proves deeper and longer than guided (steepest decline since the late 1990s per Analysis JSON), adverse casualty reserve development from social inflation crystallizes, and a U.S. housing/employment downturn pressures the Mortgage segment simultaneously -- the diversification benefit fails to smooth the cycle in the way it has historically. ROE compresses to a high-single-digit/low-double-digit trough and the market de-rates the stock to roughly tangible book (1.00x) on capital-adequacy concerns.
bear.starting_pb_note: Market price-to-book at the valuation date (current_price / book_value_per_share); refreshed with the price, not judged.

sensitivity.sensitivity_note: Rows are cost of equity (%), columns are exit P/B multiple (x) -- an insurer's terminal value is driven by the exit book-value multiple, not a perpetuity growth rate, so 'terminal_growth_range' here holds the exit-P/B axis values for compatibility with the standard field name.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default 25/50/25. Not skewed further toward bear despite the flagged softening reinsurance cycle, because Arch's Mortgage segment (12% of revenue, high-margin, credit-cycle rather than cat-cycle driven) and disciplined multi-segment capital rotation provide a demonstrated earnings floor through prior soft markets, and the balance sheet (~$27B total capital, A+/A1-range ratings) carries no near-term solvency or refinancing risk that would justify a heavier bear weight. UNCHANGED in this update.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street bases coincide: this is a book-value model with no SBC add-back, so the band has collapsed.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Arch is valued as a book-value compounding machine, not a cash-flow-generating operating company. The three segments (Insurance, Reinsurance, Mortgage) earn underwriting profit plus investment income on float; that profit either gets paid out as a nominal common dividend (~4% payout -- Arch has historically preferred buybacks to dividends) or retained and compounded into book value, with a further layer of per-share value creation from buying back stock below its eventual exit multiple. The model therefore projects common BVPS forward year by year from ROE and the buyback-funded share count, and prices the business as the present value of (small) interim dividends plus a Year-5 exit at an assumed price-to-book multiple, discounted at the cost of equity. This mirrors the Fairfax Financial (FRFHF) precedent in the user's memory and is the correct family of model per the dcf-methods routing table's 'Insurer, holdco, compounder-of-book' row.
key_risks_to_valuation: Property-catastrophe reinsurance pricing is softening sharply into 2026-2027 renewals (up to 25% risk-adjusted rate-on-line decline at June 2026), which could push ROE below even the bear case if it proves structural rather than cyclical

Casualty reserve adequacy is a live industry-wide risk from social inflation and nuclear jury verdicts; a reserve charge would hit book value directly and is not distinguishable in this model from a bad underwriting year

The exit P/B assumption does almost all the work (>98% of intrinsic value in every scenario comes from the terminal exit price, not interim dividends) because Arch pays a nominal common dividend -- the valuation is highly sensitive to the multiple the market is willing to pay for book value in five years, which is a market-sentiment variable this model cannot forecast with precision

Buyback-price assumptions (glide from today's 1.60x to the exit multiple) are a modeling simplification; management has been price-sensitive (heavy buying near 1.4x in Q3 2026, little in October), so the actual share count and per-share compounding will differ

Mortgage segment (GSE-linked) carries external policy risk (PMIERs, FHFA/GSE reform, increased use of credit risk transfer) that is outside Arch's control and could remove the segment's diversification benefit

Leverage has risen: $2.0bn of senior notes issued in June 2026 while $3.4bn of stock was repurchased in nine months; debt plus preferred is about 19% of total capital, which narrows the cushion the bear case assumes
